sample_unit: treatment plans (42 internal test plans plus 560 national DAHANCA plans)
models_evaluated: Deep neural network dose prediction model trained on 388 head and neck radiotherapy plans

links.outcome: Dose prediction accuracy on external multi-centre data versus internal test data
links.effect: Model trained on single-centre data (388 plans) was tested on 560 external plans from six institutions. Median Dmean differences were -0.1 Gy for PTVs and 1.1 Gy for OARs across cohorts, supporting generalisability.
links.quote: Predictions closely matched clinically applied dose distributions with median D<sub>mean</sub> differences of -0.1 Gy [interquartile range -0.5, 0.3] for PTVs and 1.1 Gy [-0.6, 3.7] for OARs across cohorts.

links.outcome: Deep learning dose prediction versus a simpler median-based model on the same data
links.effect: The deep learning model outperformed the median model. OAR Dmean difference was 1.1 Gy [-0.6, 3.7] versus -4.6 Gy [-14.6, 3.9] for the median model, which had larger interquartile ranges.
links.quote: The dose prediction model outperformed the median-based model, with prediction-plan differences within interquartile ranges observed across cohorts, supporting generalisability.

screen.reason: Multicenter external validation of deep learning dose prediction for radiotherapy planning without testing specific deployment workflows or governance practices.
